entries.value: Domaine Faiveley Bourgogne Rouge 2022 is Pinot Noir under Burgundy’s regional name, from a family house in Nuits-Saint-Georges. entries.target: wine:Marcel Lapierre Morgon 2023
entries.value: Marcel Lapierre Morgon 2023 is cru Beaujolais, Gamay from the family’s old vines at Villié-Morgon. It ferments in whole bunches with native yeasts and little or no added sulphur, giving crushed strawberry, cherry and a floral lift, silky, with very low tannin and bright acidity. With so little tannin, the soft-boiled egg and hollandaise of the Eggs Owen stay sweet while the fruit meets the red wine-braised short rib débris: our value bottle for that plate. We pour it lightly chilled, 55 to 59°F, in a Burgundy bowl, never decanted. The late Marcel Lapierre led Beaujolais back to natural winemaking, and his children run the estate now.

entries.value: Jean Foillard Côte du Py Morgon 2022 is Gamay grown on the hill at the centre of Morgon, its decomposed schist unlike the granite of other crus. It ferments long and cool in whole bunches with native yeasts and rests in old Burgundy barrels. Dark cherry, plum and violet carry a stony, savoury edge, deeper than the usual Beaujolais, and soft tannin meets the tasso, Creole sauce and pimento cheese grit cake: our classic bottle for the New Orleans Shrimp & Grits. entries.target: wine:Domaine Jean Grivot Echézeaux Grand Cru 2011
entries.value: Domaine Jean Grivot Echézeaux Grand Cru 2011 is Pinot Noir from the slope above the Clos de Vougeot in Flagey-Echézeaux, made classical and firm, with moderate new oak, by a Vosne-Romanée family. Fifteen years on: dark cherry, rose and spice, forest floor arriving, silky and layered. Our celebration bottle for the Roasted Rohan Duck Breast, it has fruit for the glazed peaches and a savoury side for the candied hazelnuts.
